status: one-seed z-only representation diagnostic; not a headline result
interpretation: Moving from one goal vector to four does not improve held-out task exact match in this first pilot.
The multi-vector latent modestly improves correct-versus-shuffled separation, zero-goal sensitivity, random-goal sensitivity, and held-out linear probe accuracy.
The result supports the idea that richer latent capacity helps goal decodability and causal leverage, but not yet enough to pass the strong z-only gate.
Because task quality is flat while causal signatures improve, the next step should strengthen how the richer latent is used rather than expanding to large depth or horizon sweeps.
